samples.summary: `EditorAPI.getStore()` exposes `DocStore.setPageSetup`, which bypasses both `assertUsablePageSetup` and the read-only neutering of `setPageSetup`
samples.evidence: `getStore: () => docStore` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2866) is public on `EditorAPI` (interface at editor.ts:55) and is already used from the frontend (`docs-export-button.tsx:53` calls `editor.getStore().getDocument()`). `DocStore.setPageSetup` (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:28; `MemDocStore` at packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:98, `YorkieDocStore` at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2710) performs no validation, takes no snapshot, and triggers no `doc.refresh()`/relayout/render. So `editor.getStore().setPageSetup(bad)` reaches the CRDT with hostile geometry, with no undo entry and a stale layout — and it still does so on a read-only mount, where `initialize()` only replaces the `api.setPageSetup` entry (editor.ts:3915). No in-tree caller does this today, which is why this is a latent bypass rather than a live bug; the design doc that asserts the opposite is `docs/design/docs/docs-pagination.md:350` ("there is no second way to write a page setup").

samples.summary: The docs content PUT endpoint writes `pageSetup` into the CRDT with only a shape guard, bypassing the new write-path validation
samples.evidence: `putContent` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:127-180) validates the body with `assertValidDocsBody` (which the comment says covers only "the fields the writer unconditionally dereferences") and then hands the whole body to `writeDocsRoot`, which copies `document.pageSetup.paperSize` / `.margins` verbatim into the Yorkie root (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:523-528). An API-key client can therefore persist `NaN`/negative/margin-swallowing geometry for every collaborator — exactly what `assertUsablePageSetup` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:975) exists to prevent, and the path the PR's own rationale names as the reason for clamping on read. Impact is bounded by the new read clamp in `resolvePageSetup`, so the editor and both exporters survive it; what remains is a poisoned stored value that the backend then echoes back unclamped (see the related finding on `docs-tree.ts:464)`.

samples.summary: A second copy of `readPageSetup` lives in the backend and is not routed through `resolvePageSetup`, so the change's "single read path" invariant does not hold across packages
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:464` implements its own `readPageSetup` (`Number(ps?.width)` → `NaN` for a missing field, exactly the case the new resolver docstring at packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:800-830 calls out), and `readDocsRoot` assigns it raw at docs-tree.ts:441. `GET /v1/.../content` (docs-content.controller.ts:109) therefore still returns `pageSetup: { width: NaN, … }` to CLI/API consumers, and a subsequent `PUT` echoes it straight back into the CRDT. The backend site still behaves exactly as before — it is only now out of step with the invariant the docs package just tightened, and it is the one read path the new docstring's caller list omits.

samples.summary: The Page Setup dialog calls `editor.getPageSetup()` from an effect with no capability guard, while the sibling painter toggle got one (`supportsPainter`)
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-page-setup-dialog.tsx:121-127 does `if (!open || !editor) return; const current = editor.getPageSetup();` inside `useEffect`. The toolbar's `PageSetupButton` (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:817, and the mobile item at :943) is enabled for any non-null editor, so an `EditorAPI` implementation predating this change (the diff's own comment notes the frontend runs no `tsc`, every double is `as unknown as EditorAPI`, and `EditorAPI` is exported from `@wafflebase/docs` for out-of-tree adapters) throws a TypeError inside the effect when the dialog opens — the same failure mode `supportsPainter` (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:117) was added to prevent, one press later. The new test at packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/docs-format-painter-toggle.test.tsx:199 deletes `getPageSetup`/`setPageSetup` from its stub but only asserts the toolbar mounts, never that the dialog opens.

samples.summary: The ruler's margin drag now calls a write path that throws, where it previously always stored
samples.evidence: `applyDrag` (packages/docs/src/view/ruler/index.ts:385-412) checks its own 20 px slack against `this.cachedPageWidth`/`cachedPageHeight`, cached at render time from the last paginated layout (ruler/index.ts:123-124), and then invokes `marginChangeCb`, which is now `writePageSetup` → `assertUsablePageSetup` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2081). Before this change the callback could not throw. If the cached page box is ever stale relative to `doc.document.pageSetup` at the moment of the callback (a remote paper-size change landing between the render that filled the cache and the drag frame), the ruler's check passes and the assert throws a `RangeError` out of a pointer-event handler, aborting the drag mid-gesture instead of clamping. The window is narrow — the two values are refreshed together on each render — so this is a suspicion; confirming it needs a test that mutates `doc.document.pageSetup` between a ruler render and `applyDrag`.

finding.summary: `EditorAPI.getStore()` exposes `DocStore.setPageSetup`, which bypasses both `assertUsablePageSetup` and the read-only neutering of `setPageSetup`
finding.evidence: `getStore: () => docStore` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2866) is public on `EditorAPI` (interface at editor.ts:55) and is already used from the frontend (`docs-export-button.tsx:53` calls `editor.getStore().getDocument()`). `DocStore.setPageSetup` (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:28; `MemDocStore` at packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:98, `YorkieDocStore` at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2710) performs no validation, takes no snapshot, and triggers no `doc.refresh()`/relayout/render. So `editor.getStore().setPageSetup(bad)` reaches the CRDT with hostile geometry, with no undo entry and a stale layout — and it still does so on a read-only mount, where `initialize()` only replaces the `api.setPageSetup` entry (editor.ts:3915). No in-tree caller does this today, which is why this is a latent bypass rather than a live bug; the design doc that asserts the opposite is `docs/design/docs/docs-pagination.md:350` ("there is no second way to write a page setup").

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in-tree. `getStore(): DocStore` is a public EditorAPI member (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:55) implemented as an unwrapped passthrough `getStore: () => docStore` (editor.ts:2866). The guarded write path `writePageSetup` (editor.ts:2078-2090) performs `assertUsablePageSetup`, `docStore.snapshot()`, `doc.refresh()`, `invalidateLayout()` and `render()`, none of which exist in the store implementations themselves: `MemDocStore.setPageSetup` is a bare deep-copy assignment (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:98-100) and `YorkieDocStore.setPageSetup` writes directly into the CRDT root (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2710-2720). The read-only neutering loop only overwrites entries on `api`, listing `'setPageSetup'` (editor.ts:3906-3922) but not `getStore`, so `api.getStore().setPageSetup(...)` still mutates on a read-only mount. `getStore()` is demonstrably reachable outside the package (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-export-button.tsx:53, docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:470, docs-find-bar.tsx:56, packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/bridge.ts:386), so the bypass is on a reachable API surface, and the design doc's invariant "there is no second way to write a page setup" (docs/design/docs/docs-pagination.md:350) is contradicted. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, nothing guards the handed-out store, and "a new guard with a way around it" / "a violated invariant other modules assume" is exactly this lens's lane. Absence of a current in-tree caller is a confidence/latency point, not grounds to drop a guard bypass.

finding.summary: The docs content PUT endpoint writes `pageSetup` into the CRDT with only a shape guard, bypassing the new write-path validation
finding.evidence: `putContent` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:127-180) validates the body with `assertValidDocsBody` (which the comment says covers only "the fields the writer unconditionally dereferences") and then hands the whole body to `writeDocsRoot`, which copies `document.pageSetup.paperSize` / `.margins` verbatim into the Yorkie root (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:523-528). An API-key client can therefore persist `NaN`/negative/margin-swallowing geometry for every collaborator — exactly what `assertUsablePageSetup` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:975) exists to prevent, and the path the PR's own rationale names as the reason for clamping on read. Impact is bounded by the new read clamp in `resolvePageSetup`, so the editor and both exporters survive it; what remains is a poisoned stored value that the backend then echoes back unclamped (see the related finding on `docs-tree.ts:464)`.

verdict.reason: The unvalidated write is real (docs-content.controller.ts:154 validates only blocks/header/footer, and docs-tree.ts:523-528 copies pageSetup verbatim), but it is not a bypass of a guard that protects anything reachable. `assertUsablePageSetup` (editor.ts:976) guards only the in-process `EditorAPI.setPageSetup` write; the corresponding protection for writers the editor does not own is the read clamp `resolvePageSetup` (types.ts:826-857), whose docstring at types.ts:800-825 explicitly names unvalidated CRDT/import writers and states that clamping on read is the deliberate answer for "data we do not control". I grepped every consumer of a stored pageSetup and all of them go through that clamp: editor.ts:1392/2094/2456/2993/3700, pdf-exporter.ts:96, docx-exporter.ts:168, store/memory.ts:95, frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:661-666, cli/paginate.ts:26. NaN/negative/margin-swallowing geometry stored by this endpoint is substituted with defaults at every layout, render and export sink, so nothing at the bypassing site fails, crashes, loses data, or defeats a permission guard. The finding itself concedes this and defers its only residual (the unclamped backend echo at docs-tree.ts:464) to a separate finding that remains in the gate. The reviewer's description is also inaccurate in detail: there is no pageSetup "shape guard" in assertValidDocsBody at all, and the backend never was a caller of EditorAPI, so the assert never covered this path.

finding.summary: The ruler's margin drag now calls a write path that throws, where it previously always stored
finding.evidence: `applyDrag` (packages/docs/src/view/ruler/index.ts:385-412) checks its own 20 px slack against `this.cachedPageWidth`/`cachedPageHeight`, cached at render time from the last paginated layout (ruler/index.ts:123-124), and then invokes `marginChangeCb`, which is now `writePageSetup` → `assertUsablePageSetup` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2081). Before this change the callback could not throw. If the cached page box is ever stale relative to `doc.document.pageSetup` at the moment of the callback (a remote paper-size change landing between the render that filled the cache and the drag frame), the ruler's check passes and the assert throws a `RangeError` out of a pointer-event handler, aborting the drag mid-gesture instead of clamping. The window is narrow — the two values are refreshed together on each render — so this is a suspicion; confirming it needs a test that mutates `doc.document.pageSetup` between a ruler render and `applyDrag`.

verdict.reason: The wiring is as described (ruler/index.ts:385-412 -> editor.ts:2093-2097 -> assertUsablePageSetup at editor.ts:976-1013), but the throw is unreachable from the ruler drag. (a) The ruler's guard uses the same quantity the assert uses: cachedPageWidth/Height come from paginateLayout's getEffectiveDimensions(resolvePageSetup(doc.document.pageSetup)) (pagination.ts:52-69,184-185; editor.ts:1392-1407; ruler/index.ts:121-125), and the ruler's 20 px floor strictly dominates the assert's MIN_CONTENT_PX = 1 (types.ts:763; editor.ts:1003-1012), with margins clamped >= 0 (ruler/index.ts:402-405) and cachedPageWidth initialised to 0 so an unrendered ruler rejects every drag. (b) The claimed staleness window does not exist: doc.document is a snapshot updated only by Doc.refresh() (document.ts:105-110,123-125; memory.ts:41-43 clones), and every refresh in the docs editor is followed synchronously by render() -> paint() -> ruler.render() in the same task (editor.ts:2087-2089, 2169/2194, 2201, 3842/3851; docs-view.tsx:378-394 for remote changes), so no mouseup task can observe a cache stale relative to doc.document.pageSetup. The only path skipping ruler.render (scaleFactor < 1, editor.ts:2044) is exactly the path where ruler.hide() removes the drag surface (editor.ts:1571-1577). What remains is a duplicated constant (20 vs MIN_CONTENT_PX) that could drift - minor, not the reachable RangeError out of a pointer handler this finding grades major.

finding.summary: `serializeMarkdown`'s new URL allowlist + newline fold silently changes the output of two existing out-of-diff consumers (the docs CLI and the slides CLI)
finding.evidence:
`packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:129` (`wafflebase docs content --format md`) and `packages/cli/src/slides/content.ts:184` both call the same `serializeMarkdown`. The diff changes its contract in two ways neither call site was reviewed against: 1. `URI_CHARS = /^[A-Za-z0-9\-._~:/?#[\]@!$&'()*+,;=%^@-￿]+$/` refuses any destination containing a character RFC 3986 leaves out — `|`, `{`, `}`, `^`, `"`, `` ` ``, `\`. Those appear in real, benign URLs (e.g. Google Fonts `?family=Roboto|Open+Sans`, templated links, unencoded `{id}` paths). Previously such an href was emitted verbatim; now `isEmittableUrl` returns false and the link degrades to bare text — the URL is *deleted* from CLI output with no diagnostic. An image `src` in the same shape becomes `[image]`, losing the source entirely. 2. `escapeMarkdownText` now folds `\r\n^E  ` to a space. The diff's own comment records that a run-internal `\n` is the model's *soft line break* (DOCX ``, PPTX ``, HTML `
` in a cell). The slides CLI path (`slides/content.ts:184`) serializes `TextBody.blocks` where `` is common, so previously-multi-line CLI output is now single-line. No CLI test asserts on link output (`packages/cli/test/docs-content.test.ts`, `slides-content.test.ts` have no `](` expectations), so nothing downstream will flag the drift, and the CLI docs describing `--format md` were not updated.

verdict.reason: The blast-radius premise ("neither call site was reviewed against the new contract", "no CLI test asserts on link output", "CLI docs not updated") is contradicted by the repository. packages/cli/test/docs-content.test.ts:153-239 is a suite written specifically because `docs content --format md` is a separate consumer of the serializer's URL gate, and it asserts on `](` output at :173, :182, :191, :217-221, :237; packages/cli/test/slides-content.test.ts:240-266 does the same for `slides content --format md`, naming it "the second consumer" and pinning `[Report](/uploads/report.pdf)`/`[Home](https://example.com/)`. docs/design/cli.md:763-764 (§6.5, the doc for `--format md`) documents the new rule verbatim, including the RFC-3986-only destination requirement and that a rejected image source becomes `[image]`. What remains true — that URI_CHARS (markdown.ts:282) excludes `|`/`{`/`}` so an odd-but-benign URL degrades to bare text, and that LINE_SEPARATORS (markdown.ts:466,480) folds soft breaks to a space — is the new guard's own designed strictness, applied uniformly to every consumer (cli/src/docs/content.ts:129, cli/src/slides/content.ts:184, frontend/src/app/docs/text-actions.ts:44), degrading gracefully under the existing LOSSY_NOTICE. No caller passes rejected arguments, bypasses the guard, or breaks; the complaint is statable without leaving the diff and belongs to the correctness/design-fit lens ("logic inside the diff", "whether the new guard is the right design"), which this lens explicitly defers.
